terms.comment: Plural aulaea, aulaeōrum n. pl., curtains (Traupman 123).
Classically a round cauldron, and the tripod of Apollo (Lewis & Short); use aulaeum or vēlum.

phrases.latin: Sed aulaeīs dīductīs nec arborēs nec montem nec lūmina vīdit
phrases.english: But when he opened the curtains he saw neither the trees nor the mountain nor the lights
phrases.source: Libellus II, Sintra: castellum et puteus

phrases.latin: Pater igitur, aulaeīs obductīs lūmineque exstīnctō, puerum amplexus, dē Arīone narrāvit
phrases.english: So Dad drew the curtains, turned off the light, put his arm round the boy and told him about Arion
phrases.source: Libellus V, Lisbōna: castellum et ōceanārium

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 123, checked against the searchable text of the book (29 October 2026).
